tasks.short: Watch for bruises, wounds, blood in urine and other signs during care, alert the nurse and record them.

steps.what: Nursing assistant observes skin, wounds, urine and intake during washing and toileting
Nursing assistant judges whether a finding needs the nurse now
Nursing assistant finds or phones the nurse to report the finding
Nurse assesses the patient and decides on treatment or a doctor's visit
Nursing assistant types the observation into the care record at shift end

tasks.design: Configure bedside observation entry in the electronic care record ({OTHER}) on a mobile device: a body map for bruises and pressure areas, a wound photo, a urine colour scale and a free note, saved at the moment of care. A 'notify nurse' option sends the entry with photo to the nurse's phone; urgent findings are still reported in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Care records were desktop screens in the office, so observations were typed from memory at shift end.
tasks.enabler_now: Care record systems run on phones and tablets with photo capture and push notifications.
tasks.still_hard: Spotting a symptom and judging its urgency is clinical observation that no form replaces; photos of patients need consent and careful storage.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing small changes in a resident they know well and deciding when something is not right.

ambition.what: Nurses who see every new skin finding with a photo the same hour, so pressure sores are treated earlier.

tasks.altitude: The assistant records at the bedside instead of at shift end; decision rights on escalation stay the same.

reach.task: Report injuries noticed while moving patients
reach.learn: Whether the same body map and notification fit transport staff.

evidence.claim: Care record systems offer mobile observation entry with body maps, photos and notifications.
Processing health data on a large scale is on the Dutch regulator's list of processing that needs a DPIA.
Software that assesses wounds from photos to support diagnosis would likely be a medical device; this design only stores photos.

assumptions: Boundary: from the care moment to the observation recorded and the nurse informed; treatment is outside.
Input contract: observation with resident ID, time, body location, type, photo and note, produced by the assistant on the mobile device; fallback is the desktop record at shift end.
No model interprets photos or symptoms.
Nurse time is outside the assistant's savings.
Observation and judgement time do not change.
unknowns: Whether the care record has a mobile app and photo capture enabled.
The facility's policy on photographing residents.
research_questions: How long after a finding does the nurse see it today?

already_counted.description: Assistant still observes and judges every finding.

incremental.description: Assistant handles device charging, logins and failed uploads.
Nurse reviews photo entries and keeps the body map categories current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On a ward where devices are shared and urgent findings dominate, assistants keep reporting in person and typing later.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with residents to learn how they feel and what help or emotional support they need.

steps.what: Nursing assistant talks with the resident about feelings and needs during care
Nursing assistant comforts, helps or arranges small support on the spot
Nursing assistant tells the nurse or family when mood or needs change
Nursing assistant types mood and wishes into the daily care report

tasks.design: Add a short wellbeing check (mood, pain, sleep, appetite, wish) to the daily report in the electronic care record ({OTHER}), with dictation for the free note. A trend rule flags a resident whose mood or pain score drops for three days and notifies the nurse; the conversation itself is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mood and wishes went into free text that nobody could trend, and typing on a desktop took time.
tasks.enabler_now: Care records support custom fields and simple rules, and phone dictation handles Dutch.
tasks.still_hard: Trust and comfort come from the conversation; dictation in Dutch may still make errors that need checking.
tasks.human_edge: Earning a resident's trust, noticing loneliness or fear and responding with warmth.

ambition.what: A weekly look at each resident's wellbeing trend in the care team meeting.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; the assistant's observations reach the nurse as a trend, not only as a remark.

reach.task: Talk with clients at home about their needs
reach.learn: Whether the same five-field check works in home care.

evidence.claim: Dictation supports Dutch (Netherlands) as a preview language with spoken punctuation; preview languages may be less accurate.
Care records can hold custom fields and trigger notifications on simple trend rules.
Large-scale processing of health data needs a DPIA in the Netherlands.

assumptions: Boundary: from the conversation to the report recorded and the nurse informed; care planning is outside.
Input contract: daily wellbeing check with resident ID, date and five scored fields plus note, produced by the assistant; fallback is free text.
Dictation runs within the care record or a service covered by the facility's DPIA.
Nurse and family time is outside the assistant's savings.
unknowns: Whether the care record allows custom fields and rules.
Whether residents or families object to scored wellbeing fields.
research_questions: Do trend flags reach the nurse earlier than spoken reports do?

already_counted.description: Assistant still has the conversation and gives support.

incremental.description: Assistant corrects dictation errors and fills the five fields consistently.
Nurse reviews trend flags and tunes the rule.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where assistants already write short reports, the saving is only the faster entry; the conversation is most of the time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure temperature, blood pressure, pulse and breathing as ordered, record them and report abnormal values.

steps.what: Nurse sets which vital signs to measure and how often
Nursing assistant measures temperature, blood pressure, pulse and respiration at the bedside
Nursing assistant writes readings on a paper round list
Nursing assistant types the readings into the care record
Nursing assistant works out the early warning score and judges the patient
Nursing assistant reports abnormal readings to the nurse

tasks.design: Connected vital-signs monitors send each reading to the electronic care record ({OTHER}) after the assistant scans the resident's wristband or room code and confirms the values on the device. The record computes the early warning score from the facility's chart and notifies the nurse above the threshold; the assistant still raises concerns the score misses.
tasks.previous_blocker: Monitors and the care record were not linked, so readings went via paper and were typed twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Spot-check monitors with network links and care records that accept device readings are common in hospitals and reaching care homes.
tasks.still_hard: Device purchase, Wi-Fi coverage and patient matching cost money and time; measuring stays hands-on.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a resident looks unwell even when the numbers are normal, and measuring calmly with anxious residents.

ambition.what: Early warning scores visible to the nurse within a minute of each round, so deterioration is caught between rounds.

tasks.altitude: The assistant measures and confirms instead of copying and calculating; escalation rights stay with the nurse.

reach.task: Take vital signs before a consultation
reach.learn: Whether the same monitor link and confirmation step fit an outpatient room.

evidence.claim: Networked spot-check monitors can send readings to an electronic record after patient identification.
Large-scale processing of health data needs a DPIA in the Netherlands.
Software that computes clinical scores to guide care may fall under medical device rules; using the score chart already in the care record avoids new classification.

assumptions: Boundary: from the nurse's order to readings recorded and abnormal values reported; treatment is outside.
Input contract: reading with resident ID from wristband or room code, time, device ID and values, produced by the monitor; fallback is manual entry in the care record.
The early warning chart is the one the facility already uses; no model scores patients.
Nurse time is outside the assistant's savings.
unknowns: Whether the facility's monitors can be networked and the care record accepts device data.
How many residents need vitals more than once a day.
research_questions: How many transcription errors occur in vital signs today?

already_counted.description: Assistant confirms device readings belong to the right resident.

incremental.description: Assistant charges devices, pairs them and handles failed uploads.
Nurse checks notifications and tunes thresholds per resident.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wards where only some monitors link, or Wi-Fi drops, keep paper lists for part of the round.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Learn each resident's condition, care plan and activities from the handover, the record, nurses and family.

steps.what: Nurse prepares the shift handover from the care record and leads it

loop.input: Free-text daily reports and observations of the last 24 hours per resident, plus care plan changes and due tasks from the care record.
loop.output: Three to six bullets per resident, each linked to the report it comes from.
loop.check: Each bullet must cite a report of that resident inside the window; doses, times and values must appear verbatim in the cited report; every item on the deterministic flag list (falls, new wounds, scores above threshold, medication changes) must appear, else the resident is marked 'read full reports'.
loop.stop: One draft and one retry per resident; on failure the resident shows the flag list and raw reports; nurse review before handover.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports are free text written by many staff; a field list covers due tasks and flags but not what happened in the narrative.

steps.what: Nursing assistant listens at the handover and asks about residents
Nursing assistant writes notes on the paper handover sheet
Nursing assistant reads care plans and latest reports for assigned residents
Nursing assistant asks the nurse or therapist about unclear treatment instructions
Nurse or therapist explains the treatment plan or allowed activities
Nursing assistant asks family carers about habits and wishes during visits

tasks.design: Before each shift the electronic care record ({OTHER}) builds a per-resident handover sheet: due care tasks, vitals, appointments, diet and mobility come from fields, and a bounded model step drafts short bullets from the last 24 hours of free-text reports, each linked to its source. The nurse checks and corrects the sheet before the handover; assistants work from that approved version on their device, add their own notes, and open the linked reports when they need detail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handover depended on the nurse reading every report and on paper notes, because free text could not be summarised reliably.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can draft short summaries of clinical text, and a field list plus source links lets the nurse check them quickly.
tasks.still_hard: AI summaries can miss points or invent details, so the check and the nurse's review cannot be skipped; health data needs a DPIA and a contract with the model provider.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the right follow-up question, and hearing from family what never reaches the record.

ambition.what: Every shift starts from the full last-24-hours picture of each resident, including weekend and night shifts with fewer nurses.

tasks.altitude: The assistant starts the shift with a checked sheet and spends less time reading reports; the nurse leads a shorter handover focused on flagged residents.

reach.task: Learn which patients need help moving and how
reach.learn: Whether mobility fields from the same sheet are enough for transport staff.

evidence.claim: Three Belgian hospital groups give patients an AI plain-language version of medical reports next to the original, without doctor review.
AI summaries of letters can miss points and make up answers.
Large-scale processing of health data and use of new technology need a DPIA in the Netherlands.
A handover summary that does not suggest diagnoses or treatment is unlikely to be a medical device or an Annex III high-risk system.

assumptions: Boundary: from handover preparation to the assistant knowing each resident's plan for the shift; care delivery is outside.

Input contract: per resident the care plan tasks due, latest vitals and scores, appointments, diet, mobility aids and free-text reports of 24 hours, produced by staff in the care record; fallback is the nurse's spoken handover and the full reports.
The model runs under a processing agreement inside the facility's environment; no data goes to consumer services.
Nurse and therapist time is outside the assistant's savings; the nurse's review time is in s1.
Talking with family does not change.
unknowns: Whether the care record can export reports to a governed model service.
How long handovers take today and who attends.
research_questions: How often does a draft miss a flagged event, measured against the nurse's corrections over four weeks?

already_counted.description: Nurse reviews and corrects the drafted handover sheet.

incremental.description: Assistant reports summary errors and missing items to the nurse.
Care record administrator monitors the summary check, flag list and model cost.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wards where nurses keep the full spoken handover see only the reading and note-taking savings; frequent check failures send assistants back to full reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nursing assistant keeps the hands-on care, observation and conversation; copying readings, typing from memory and reading every report shrink.
reach: Orderlies' reporting of injuries and mobility needs
skills_to_grow: Recording observations precisely at the bedside
Checking device readings and summaries against what they see
Explaining a concern to the nurse with the data at hand
role.ambitious_version: A nursing assistant whose bedside records and trend flags let nurses act the same hour, and who starts every shift from a checked picture of each resident.
